basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 26.' and it opens 'Vers. 26. Faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram. Cum caetera jubendo'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 26. Faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram. Cum caetera jubendo fecerit, quasi maximam rem facturus Deus et cunctis quae | fecerat praeferendam, quasi quodam concilio dicit: Faciamus. Quod, licet quidam ad angelos referendum dicant, melius tamen ad sanctam Trinitatem refertur.
